subject: Chemistry
topic: Aldehydes vs ketones: naming and structure
title: Aldehyde or Ketone? Structure and IUPAC Names
summary: Methanal and propanone both have C=O, yet one is an aldehyde and one a ketone. Where the C=O sits decides it, and the names follow: -al for aldehydes, -one for ketones, plus the common names.

notes.title: 03 – Aldehydes vs Ketones: Naming and Structure

keyPoints: **Aldehyde**: an H on the carbonyl carbon, so C=O sits at the **end** of the chain (R–CHO).
**Ketone**: carbon groups on both sides, so C=O sits **inside** the chain (R–CO–R′).
IUPAC: alkane − e + **al** (methanal, ethanal, propanal; the CHO carbon is C-1, no locant); alkane − e + **one** (propanone, butanone, pentan-2-one, pentan-3-one).
Common names: **formaldehyde**, **acetaldehyde**; **dimethyl ketone = acetone**. The smallest ketone, propanone, has three carbons.
